version.changelog:
Initial release of Agentify: a tool to analyze, improve, and standardize web pages for agent, scraper, and automation usability.

- Analyzes web pages or code for agent-friendliness, scoring across 9 technical categories with detailed reports
- Automatically rewrites web templates to add semantic markup, accessibility features (ARIA), structured data, and automation-friendly selectors (e.g., data-testid), preserving all existing logic and appearance
- Generates agent-friendly design spec documents tailored for development teams, including code-style guidance, migration plans, and component checklists
- Supports multiple frameworks (HTML, JSX, Vue, Svelte) and integrates with automation tools (Playwright, Puppeteer, Cypress, Selenium)
- Provides structured workflows, safety rules, and knowledge base references for consistency and best practices

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agentify
Version: 1.0.0

The 'agentify' skill bundle is a legitimate tool designed to improve web page accessibility and machine-readability for AI agents and scrapers. It includes comprehensive documentation and instructions for auditing code (Analyze), non-destructively updating templates with semantic HTML and ARIA attributes (Rewrite), and generating design standards (Design Spec). The instructions in SKILL.md include explicit safety rules to preserve existing logic and formatting, and there are no indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or unauthorized system access.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions are internally consistent with its stated purpose of auditing and improving sites for agent/scraper friendliness; it reads and modifies project files and fetches pages, which matches its remit and no unrelated credentials or installers are requested.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (make pages agent-friendly) match the instructions and included references: the skill fetches URLs, reads files/globs, scans project files (package.json, components), and can produce or write a spec—these are proportionate to an auditing/rewriting tool. No unrelated environment variables, binaries, or installers are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent to fetch URLs, read files by path/glob/IDE selection, grep the repo, read representative components, perform in-place transformations (Rewrite workflow), and write an output spec file. This is expected, but it means the agent will access and may modify repository files—users should expect file reads/writes and review diffs before accepting changes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no bundled code. Nothing will be downloaded or written by an installer step beyond what the agent is instructed to do at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested. The only data access described is project files and fetched web pages, which is appropriate for a tool that audits and rewrites code and content.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default autonomous invocation are set. The skill expects to read and modify files and to write an agent-friendly-spec.md; while this is coherent, users should be aware the agent can perform file edits when invoked. There is no request for persistent / global privileges or to modify other skills or agent config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it will fetch pages and scan or modify files in a project (add attributes, insert JSON-LD, and write a spec). Before installing or running it on important repositories: 1) Run it in a safe/isolated copy of your repo first; 2) Require a human review step (diff) before applying edits; 3) Avoid pointing it at folders containing secrets or build artifacts you don't want scanned; 4) If you have CI/CD or tests, run them after changes; 5) If you want to restrict network access, be aware it may fetch URLs when auditing live pages. These are operational precautions rather than contradictions in the skill itself.
